data.hypothesis: The measured unroll variants are all slower than the 55.00 µs baseline: two groups measured 82.32 µs, three groups 147.64 µs, four groups 63.81 µs, and eight groups 81.30 µs. This candidate tests whether a two-group schedule that validates and commits the first group before committing the second limits live values and register pressure enough to outperform the current four-group schedule, while still overlapping two scalar lookup chains. The prior two-group result makes a speedup uncertain; no speedup is assumed.

memory_lessons.applicability: Scalar decode-loop scheduling on this target; measurements, not unroll factor alone, should determine which schedule is retained.
memory_lessons.claim: The measured two-, three-, four-, and eight-group unroll candidates were all slower than baseline; four groups was the closest, at 63.81 µs versus 55.00 µs.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this two-group immediate-commit schedule with the same correctness and native-timing protocol before drawing conclusions.

data.notes: No commands were run and this candidate has not been locally validated or timed. The controller should validate short and empty inputs, group-boundary lengths, all padding cases, randomized valid inputs, and the official Lena input before repeated native timing.
transformations: Replaced the four-block fast-loop schedule with two independent eight-character scalar blocks and a 21-character guard, leaving at least five input characters for the existing tail/padding path.
Interleaved the two blocks' table lookups, then validated, packed, and committed each block in order; if either block is invalid, the unchanged scalar path resumes at the first unconsumed input.
Preserved the bytewise decoder for padding, invalid input, and tails, with no explicit SIMD, parallel execution, thread-budget changes, or benchmark-length specialization.
